# The dual-pane file manager for your Mac.

Source: https://diptychon.com/

Keyboard-first · macOS

Two folders side by side, so you see where a file is and where it's going. One keystroke moves it across. Every action is undoable.

2.7 MB download · 9 MB installed

Two panels, one workspace. Select a file in the left panel, press ⌥⌘→, it lands in the right. No dragging, no new windows.

Diptychon is free while in beta. Tried it? The picks below decide what gets built next — and your email is the way back to you when it ships changes, no newsletter, nothing else.

While you're here: what would make Diptychon a must-have for you?

Optional — it decides what gets built first. Skipping changes nothing.

Read by a human, steers the roadmap. Talk soon.

Apple Silicon & Intel · macOS 13+ · native Swift

Why it's different

### See everything. Undo anything.

Both panes show where files come from and where they go. A staging area collects them before you act. Every move, copy, rename and trash is reversible: multi-level ⌘Z, with a toast that says exactly what was undone.

### Small, native, private.

Native Swift, 2.7 MB to download. No telemetry, no account, no subscription: everything runs on your Mac. Free while in beta.

### Rides the Mac, not against it.

Real Finder tags that round-trip both ways. Finder's own conventions for copy, paste, go-to-folder and Quick Look, so your muscle memory just transfers.

Every command, one place

Finder conventions where they exist; chords where they earn their keep. Every key is rebindable — nothing to relearn. And when a command is missing, add your own: gadgets hand the current selection to any app or CLI tool, no plugin runtime to learn.

Compare

There's no clear winner among Mac file managers — Marta, ForkLift, Nimble Commander and Path Finder are all genuinely good. We compared them honestly, including where they beat Diptychon. Read the comparison →

Coming from one tool in particular? Marta · ForkLift · Path Finder · Total Commander on a Mac

# Diptychon vs Marta, ForkLift, Nimble & Path Finder

Source: https://diptychon.com/vs

Compare · macOS file managers

There's no clear winner among Mac file managers. This segment tool-hops for a reason. Here's an honest read of where Diptychon fits, and where these (genuinely good) tools still beat it.

Diptychon is a fast, keyboard-first dual-panel file manager: native, ~2.7 MB, no telemetry, undo anything. It's in beta — free to download while it is. This page is about fit, not a claim that it's finished.

By Till von Krueger · published 2026-07-11, last updated 2026-08-11 · competitor figures verified against vendor pages 2026-07-11

| Price model | free while in beta (pricing not set) | free | one-time $19.95 | free / $29.99 one-time Pro | subscription $32.95/yr |
| Footprint (download) | 2.7 MB | 10.7 MB | 16.3 MB | 15.0 MB | 19.4 MB |
| Native / open-source | Swift, native | Swift, native | Swift, native | C++, open-source | native |
| Dual-pane | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Undo a file operation | Yes, multi-level | No | Partial (undocumented) | No | Partial (moves) |
| Remembers your session | Yes | Yes | Yes (setting) | Yes | Partial (manual save) |
| Batch rename | Yes | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Remote (SFTP / WebDAV) | No | No | Yes | Yes | limited |

**Sources & verification, 2026-07-11 (every number linked)**

Download sizes for Marta (10.7 MB), ForkLift (16.3 MB) and Path Finder (19.4 MB) via MacUpdate; Nimble Pro $29.99 and Marta free as of 2026-07-07. Diptychon's 2.7 MB is the zip of the current notarized build, measured 2026-08-10. Prices change. Check the vendor before you buy.

Undo & session, verified 2026-07-11: Marta has no file-operation undo (open request since 2018) but documented session restore; ForkLift's release notes show undo for Trash & Multi-Rename, full scope undocumented, restore via its "Restore Windows and Tabs on Startup" setting; Nimble Commander's manual documents no undo, session restore is on by default; Path Finder added an "undo panel" for moves, extent undocumented, and layout restore is a manual "Save As Default". Diptychon's undo is multi-level across move, copy, trash and rename; overwrites are destructive and excluded. Batch rename: documented for ForkLift (Multi-Rename), Nimble Commander (Batch Rename) and Path Finder (Batch Renaming); Marta's file-operations reference lists only single-item rename. Diptychon's batch rename covers Finder-style modes (replace, add text, format with counter, change case) as one undoable operation; regex patterns are planned.

## Where each one wins (honestly)

### Marta

Wins: free, keyboard-cult-favorite, native and plain-fast.

Diptychon's edge: undo-anything and real Finder tags.

### ForkLift 4

Wins: the remote powerhouse (SFTP/FTP/WebDAV/S3/cloud/SMB), folder sync, multi-rename.

Diptychon's edge: built keyboard-first: every action has a binding, one chord moves files between panels, all in a 2.7 MB download.

### Nimble Commander

Wins: raw C++ speed, 100+ hotkeys, remote mounts, open-source.

Diptychon's edge: gentler to learn (Nimble's curve is steep), undo, native Finder tags. No feature paywall, and free while in beta.

### Path Finder

Wins: the deepest, kitchen-sink power-feature set, still actively maintained.

Diptychon's edge: free while in beta, and planned without a yearly subscription ($32.95/yr).

**Diptychon is for you if…**

- You live in the keyboard and Finder feels slow.
- You want native + tiny, not a web wrapper.
- No subscription, no telemetry matters to you.
- You mostly work on local (or mounted) drives.
- Alternatives to Marta
- Alternatives to ForkLift
- Alternatives to Path Finder
- Total Commander on a Mac

This page cedes what the others do better on purpose. If Diptychon fits, download the free beta and see for yourself.

# Is there a Total Commander for Mac?

Source: https://diptychon.com/total-commander-for-mac

Switching · Windows → macOS

No — Total Commander is Windows-only. Christian Ghisler has never shipped a macOS build, and there is no official port planned. You have two routes: run the Windows version through a compatibility layer (Wine, CrossOver) or a Windows VM, or switch to a file manager built natively for the Mac.

The compatibility route keeps your muscle memory but gives up native Finder integration, retina rendering and Apple Silicon performance. The native route means learning a new tool, but every native Mac dual-pane manager below gives you the thing you actually came for: two directories side by side, keyboard-driven.

Written 2026-08-02, updated 2026-08-11 · competitor figures verified 2026-07-11 · Diptychon is pre-1.0, under active development — free download while in beta

|  | Diptychon | Marta | ForkLift 4 | Nimble Commander | Path Finder |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Two panels side by side | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Keyboard-driven workflow | Every action bound | Yes | Partial, mouse-forward | 100+ hotkeys | Partial |
| FTP / SFTP built in | No — local-only in v1 | No | Yes | Yes | Limited |
| Plugin ecosystem | No — gadgets instead | Yes | No | No | Modules |
| Price model | free while in beta (pricing not set) | free | one-time $19.95 | free / $29.99 one-time Pro | subscription $32.95/yr |
| Download size | 2.7 MB | 10.7 MB | 16.3 MB | 15.0 MB | 19.4 MB |
| Available today | Yes — free beta | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

**Sources & verification (read this before trusting a number)**

Prices and download sizes verified 2026-07-11 against the vendors: ForkLift $19.95 (binarynights.com) · Path Finder $32.95 / 1-year licence (cocoatech.io) · Nimble Commander free & open-source, 15.0 MB (GitHub release asset). Sizes for Marta (10.7 MB), ForkLift (16.3 MB) and Path Finder (19.4 MB) via MacUpdate; Nimble Pro $29.99 and Marta free as of 2026-07-07. Diptychon's 2.7 MB is the measured zip of the current notarized build (2026-08-10).

Total Commander's platform support is per the vendor: the ghisler.com download page lists Windows (and a separate Android app) only. Prices change and vendors re-price without notice — check the vendor's own page before you buy anything here.

## Questions people actually ask

### Can I run Total Commander on a Mac with Wine or CrossOver?

Yes, and people do. Total Commander is a small, old-school Win32 application, which is the class of software Wine handles best. You give up native menu-bar integration, Finder tag and Quick Look support, and you take on a compatibility layer to maintain. A Windows VM (Parallels, VMware, UTM) is the more reliable version of the same trade — heavier, but it behaves like Windows because it is Windows.

Worth being clear about the trade: this route is right if you depend on specific Total Commander plugins. If you mainly want the two-panel workflow, a native tool will be faster and less fragile.

### Which Mac file manager is closest to Total Commander?

Depends which part of Total Commander you mean:

- The keyboard-first two-panel core → Marta or Nimble Commander. Both are native, both are free to start with.
- The built-in FTP/SFTP and archive handling → ForkLift 4 or Nimble Commander. This is the part Total Commander users miss most.
- The plugin ecosystem → nothing on macOS matches it. Marta has plugins, but it is a smaller ecosystem.

Double Commander and muCommander are also worth a look: both are free, open-source and cross-platform, which makes them the most literal ports of the idea — at the cost of not feeling especially Mac-native.

### Do the F5 / F6 copy and move keys work on a Mac?

Not out of the box in Finder, and not identically anywhere. macOS reserves the function-key row for system features by default, so most Mac dual-pane managers use their own bindings rather than reproducing Total Commander's F-key layout literally. Nimble Commander is the closest to the classic Commander key map.

Diptychon uses a modifier chord instead of a function key: ⌥⌘→ sends the selection to the other panel, ⌥⌘← pulls it back. Different keys, same one-keystroke idea.

### Is there a free Total Commander alternative for Mac?

Yes. Marta is free (though not open source), and Nimble Commander is free and open source, with a paid Pro tier for admin/root operations. Double Commander and muCommander are free and open source as well. None of them costs anything to try, so the honest advice is to try the free ones before paying for anything.

### Where does Diptychon fit?

Diptychon is a native macOS dual-panel manager built keyboard-first: two panels, one chord to send files across, multi-level undo on move, copy, trash and rename, real Finder tags, and a 2.7 MB download. It is free while in beta — final pricing is not set — and it collects no telemetry.

What it does not do matters for anyone coming from Total Commander, and the reasons differ — worth separating, because one of them is permanent and the others are not:

- No FTP or SFTP. A deliberate boundary: v1 is local-only, and the app is built so it stays small. The internal seam that a remote source would plug into exists, but nothing is promised and nothing is scheduled.
- No plugin runtime — gadgets instead. Not an omission, a different answer to the same need: a gadget hands the current selection to any app or CLI tool you name, with no plugin API to learn and nothing to install. Narrower than Total Commander's plugins, and it already ships.
- No archive browsing. Not in v1. It is parked as a known gap rather than scheduled — it gets built if the people using the beta ask for it, and dropped if they don't.

Diptychon is pre-1.0 and under active development, so this list is a snapshot, not a verdict. But do not pick a tool on a roadmap: if built-in FTP or a plugin ecosystem is why you use Total Commander today, ForkLift or Nimble Commander is the honest answer. For the local dual-pane core, the Diptychon beta is a free download.

**Come to Diptychon from Total Commander if…**

- You want the two-panel workflow, not the plugin ecosystem.
- You work on local and mounted drives, not remote servers.
- You want native and tiny, not Wine or a VM.
- You want undo on file operations — Total Commander has none.

**Stay where you are if…**

- You depend on Total Commander plugins.
- You need FTP/SFTP inside the file manager.
- You want a finished 1.0 — Diptychon is a beta.
- You want archive browsing as folders.
- Alternatives to Marta
- Alternatives to ForkLift
- Alternatives to Path Finder
- Diptychon vs all four, side by side

Diptychon is in beta — free to download, but pre-1.0. If you need every feature today, the shipping tools above are good; this page tells you which one fits.

# Looking for a Marta alternative?

Source: https://diptychon.com/marta-alternative

Compare · Marta

Marta is free, native Swift, dual-pane and genuinely fast — for most people it is the right answer, and it costs nothing to try. People go looking for an alternative for two specific reasons, and neither is about speed.

The first is continuity: Marta is a one-person project and development has come in bursts, with long quiet stretches between releases. The second is undo: Marta has no undo for file operations — the request has been open since 2018. Its documentation describes delete as permanent. Batch rename is also absent; the file-operations reference lists single-item rename only.

Written 2026-08-02, updated 2026-08-11 · competitor figures verified 2026-07-11 · Diptychon is pre-1.0, under active development — free download while in beta

|  | Marta | Diptychon | Nimble Commander | ForkLift 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Price | free (not open source) | free while in beta (pricing not set) | free / $29.99 one-time Pro | one-time $19.95 |
| Undo a file operation | No — open request since 2018 | Yes, multi-level | No | Partial (undocumented) |
| Batch rename | No | Yes, undoable | Yes | Yes |
| Finder tags | Not documented | Yes, round-trip | Not documented | Not documented |
| Remembers your session | Yes, strong | Yes | Yes, default on | Yes (setting) |
| Plugins | Yes | No | No | No |
| Download size | 10.7 MB | 2.7 MB | 15.0 MB | 16.3 MB |
| Available today | Yes | Yes — free beta | Yes | Yes |

**Sources & verification (every claim about Marta is linked)**

Undo: Marta has no file-operation undo — issue #230 has been open since 2018, with #705 as a later duplicate; the docs describe delete as permanent. Batch rename: Marta's file-operations reference lists single-item Rename (⇧F6) only. Session restore: documented and automatic — windows, tabs, folders and cursor position (reset doc). Verified 2026-07-11.

Price and size: Marta free and 10.7 MB via MacUpdate, checked 2026-07-07/11 (marta.sh does not show a price). Diptychon's 2.7 MB is the measured zip of the current notarized build (2026-08-10). "Not documented" in the Finder-tags row means exactly that — the vendor's docs do not cover it, and we are not going to assert a competitor lacks a feature we could not verify.

## Questions people actually ask

### Is Marta still being maintained?

Yes, but in bursts. Marta is developed by a single developer, and its release history has long quiet stretches followed by a new version. That pattern is the single most common worry raised about it in Mac power-user communities — not capability, not speed. If a one-person project with irregular releases is a risk you are comfortable with, it is not a reason to leave.

### Does Marta have undo?

No. There is no undo for file operations. The request has been open since 2018, and Marta's own documentation describes deletion as permanent. In practice this means a mis-aimed move or delete in a keyboard-driven tool is not recoverable from inside the app.

This is the single clearest functional gap between Marta and Diptychon. Diptychon's undo is multi-level across move, copy, trash and rename. Overwrites are the documented exception — they destroy the original and cannot be reversed, in any tool.

### Does Marta have batch rename?

No. Marta's file-operations reference documents single-item rename (⇧F6) only. ForkLift, Nimble Commander and Path Finder all have a batch rename; Diptychon has one too, with Finder-style modes (replace, add text, format with a counter, change case) applied as a single undoable operation. Regex patterns are planned, not shipped.

### What is the closest alternative to Marta?

By philosophy, Nimble Commander — native, keyboard-heavy, free, and open source, so continuity is not a single-developer bet. It is faster still (C++) and has 100+ hotkeys, but the learning curve is steeper and it has no undo either.

By feel, Diptychon is the closer match: same keyboard-first two-panel model, smaller (2.7 MB vs 10.7 MB), with undo and real Finder tags added. It is free while in beta, has no plugin system, and is pre-1.0.

### Is Marta open source?

No. Marta is free but not open source — only its issue tracker is public on GitHub. Nimble Commander is the open-source option in this category.

**Switch from Marta if…**

- You have lost files to a mis-aimed move and want undo.
- You rename in batches.
- You use Finder tags and want them round-trip.
- Single-developer continuity worries you.

**Stay on Marta if…**

- You use its plugins.
- Free matters more than undo.
- You need something today.
- It already does what you need — it is good.
- Total Commander on a Mac
- Alternatives to ForkLift
- Alternatives to Path Finder
- Diptychon vs all four, side by side

Marta is free for good; Diptychon is free while in beta, with final pricing not set. If the missing undo does not bother you, stay on Marta — this page is not trying to talk you off a tool that works.

# A lighter ForkLift alternative

Source: https://diptychon.com/forklift-alternative

Compare · ForkLift

If you need remote access, ForkLift 4 is still the right answer and nothing here beats it. SFTP, FTP, WebDAV, S3, Backblaze B2, Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, SMB, AFP, NFS, plus folder sync and multi-rename — that is a genuinely deep feature set for a one-time $19.95.

People look for an alternative when they realise they never use any of it. If your files live on local and mounted drives, you are carrying a 16.3 MB remote-transfer suite to move things between two folders. The lighter native options are Marta (free), Nimble Commander (free, open source) and Diptychon (2.7 MB, free while in beta).

Written 2026-08-02, updated 2026-08-11 · competitor figures verified 2026-07-11 · Diptychon is pre-1.0, under active development — free download while in beta

|  | ForkLift 4 | Diptychon | Marta | Nimble Commander |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Remote (SFTP / WebDAV / S3) | Yes — the whole point | No | No | Yes (mounts) |
| Folder sync | Yes | No | No | Partial |
| Download size | 16.3 MB | 2.7 MB | 10.7 MB | 15.0 MB |
| Price | one-time $19.95 | free while in beta (pricing not set) | free | free / $29.99 one-time Pro |
| Keyboard-first | Partial — mouse-forward | Every action bound | Yes | 100+ hotkeys |
| Undo a file operation | Partial (Trash, Multi-Rename) | Yes, multi-level | No | No |
| Batch rename | Yes | Yes, undoable | No | Yes |
| Available today | Yes | Yes — free beta | Yes | Yes |

**Sources & verification (including what we could not re-check)**

Price verified 2026-07-11 on the vendor's own store: ForkLift $19.95 single licence (binarynights.com). Download size 16.3 MB via MacUpdate. Undo: ForkLift's release notes document undo for Trash and Multi-Rename; the full scope is not documented in the manual, which is why this page says "partial" rather than "yes" or "no". Session restore via its "Restore Windows and Tabs on Startup" setting. Batch rename documented as Multi-Rename in the same release notes.

Pending re-verification (2026-08-02): BinaryNights' licence appears to be a perpetual-use licence with a limited update window rather than a plain one-time purchase — you keep the version you bought, but a later major update needs a new licence. We could not confirm the current terms against the vendor's own page in this pass, so the table above still shows the figure verified 2026-07-11. Check binarynights.com/store before you buy.

## Questions people actually ask

### Is ForkLift a subscription?

Not in the Path Finder sense — there is no recurring charge to keep using it. As verified on the vendor's store on 2026-07-11, a single licence is a one-time $19.95. Note the caveat above: BinaryNights' model bundles a limited window of updates with the licence, so a much later major version may need a new purchase. That is materially different from a subscription, and materially different from "buy once, updated forever".

### What is a free ForkLift alternative?

Marta (free, not open source) and Nimble Commander (free and open source, with a $29.99 one-time Pro tier for admin/root operations). Nimble Commander is the one to look at if you need the remote side, since it can mount remote locations; Marta is local-only.

### Does ForkLift have undo?

Partially. Its release notes document undo for Trash and Multi-Rename operations. The manual does not document undo at all, so the full extent is unclear. We deliberately do not claim ForkLift "has no undo" — it demonstrably has some.

Diptychon's undo is multi-level and spans move, copy, trash and rename, with overwrites excluded by design because they destroy the original.

### Is ForkLift keyboard-driven?

Partly. ForkLift has shortcuts, but the workflow it is designed around is mouse-forward — drag between panels, click through remote connections. That is a reasonable design for a transfer tool. It is a different thing from a tool where every action has a binding and the mouse is optional, which is what Marta, Nimble Commander and Diptychon are.

### What does Diptychon give up compared to ForkLift?

A lot, and mostly on purpose. No remote protocols, no folder sync, no cloud-storage integration — that is a deliberate boundary, not a gap waiting to be filled, and it is the reason the download is 2.7 MB instead of 16.3 MB. Archive handling is the one genuinely open item: not in v1, parked until the people using the beta ask for it.

What you get back: every action on a key binding, multi-level undo across move, copy, trash and rename, real Finder tags, and no telemetry. Diptychon is pre-1.0 and under active development, so the feature list will grow — but it will grow inside that boundary, not across it. Both are real downloads today: ForkLift you buy, Diptychon is free while in beta.

**Look for a ForkLift alternative if…**

- You have never opened its remote features.
- You want the mouse to be optional.
- You want undo across everything, not some things.
- The footprint bothers you on principle.

**Keep ForkLift if…**

- You transfer to SFTP, S3 or WebDAV.
- You rely on folder sync.
- You want archive handling built in.
- You need it today.
- Total Commander on a Mac
- Alternatives to Marta
- Alternatives to Path Finder
- Diptychon vs all four, side by side

This page will not tell you ForkLift is bloated. It is a well-built app that does more than Diptychon ever will. The question is only whether you use the part you paid for.

# A Path Finder alternative without the subscription

Source: https://diptychon.com/path-finder-alternative

Compare · Path Finder

Path Finder is not abandoned and it is not bad — it has the deepest feature set of any Mac file manager, and version 11 shipped in February 2026. The reason people look for an alternative is the pricing model: Cocoatech moved to recurring licences, and the vendor page showed $32.95 for a one-year licence when we checked on 2026-07-11.

If the recurring charge is your reason for leaving, the one-time-purchase options are ForkLift 4 ($19.95) and Nimble Commander (free, $29.99 one-time Pro). Marta is free. Diptychon is free while in beta; its final pricing is not set.

Written 2026-08-02, updated 2026-08-11 · competitor figures verified 2026-07-11 · Diptychon is pre-1.0, under active development — free download while in beta

|  | Path Finder | Diptychon | ForkLift 4 | Nimble Commander |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Price model | recurring — $32.95 / 1-year licence | free while in beta (pricing not set) | one-time $19.95 | free / $29.99 one-time Pro |
| Download size | 19.4 MB | 2.7 MB | 16.3 MB | 15.0 MB |
| Remembers your layout | Partial — manual "Save As Default" | Yes, automatic | Yes (setting) | Yes, default on |
| Undo a file operation | Partial (moves) | Yes, multi-level | Partial (undocumented) | No |
| Keyboard-first | Partial | Every action bound | Partial | 100+ hotkeys |
| Feature depth | Deepest of the five | Deliberately narrow | Deep (remote) | Deep |
| Open source | No | No | No | Yes |
| Available today | Yes | Yes — free beta | Yes | Yes |

**Sources & verification (including what we could not re-check)**

Price verified 2026-07-11 on the vendor's own page: Path Finder $32.95, "1 Year License" (cocoatech.io). Review sites listed $29.95/yr at the time; the vendor page wins. Download size 19.4 MB via MacUpdate. Undo: Path Finder 8.5 introduced an undo panel for moves and "other undoable operations… whenever possible"; the extent is undocumented and the current knowledge base has no undo article, hence "partial". Layout: the vendor's own support site lists "Doesn't Remember Layout or Windows" among its most common issues, and layout is saved manually via Window → Save As Default.

Pending re-verification (2026-08-02): Cocoatech also offers a monthly subscription and multi-year licences, and the version numbering may have changed since v11 (February 2026). We could not reach the vendor's page in this pass, so the figures above remain the ones verified 2026-07-11. Check cocoatech.io before you buy.

## Questions people actually ask

### Is Path Finder a subscription now?

It is recurring, yes. Cocoatech moved away from a perpetual licence, and the product page showed $32.95 for a one-year licence when we checked on 2026-07-11. There is also a monthly option, and longer multi-year licences. Whichever you pick, continuing to get updates means paying again — that is the change people object to, and it is the reason this page exists.

### Is Path Finder discontinued?

No. That claim circulates because of a quiet period years ago, but version 11 shipped in February 2026 and the product is actively maintained. If you read somewhere that Path Finder is dead, that is out of date.

### Does Path Finder remember your window layout?

Only partially, and it is the complaint the vendor's own support site acknowledges — "Doesn't Remember Layout or Windows" appears among its most common issues. Layout is saved manually through Window → Save As Default, and tab sets are manual presets. There is a "last used folders" preference.

For a tool you open dozens of times a day, this is more annoying than it sounds. Diptychon persists panel paths, sort order, layout and pins automatically, with no save step. So do Marta and Nimble Commander.

### What is the best one-time-purchase alternative to Path Finder?

Depends what you use Path Finder for:

- The remote and transfer features → ForkLift 4, one-time $19.95, deeper remote support than Path Finder's.
- The power-user depth, for free → Nimble Commander, free and open source, $29.99 one-time for the Pro tier.
- Just the dual-pane workflow, keyboard-driven → Marta (free) or Diptychon (free while in beta, final pricing not set).

None of them replaces Path Finder feature-for-feature. If you use its modules, its batch tools and its browser panes together, there is no like-for-like swap — that is the honest answer.

### Is there a free Path Finder alternative?

Marta and Nimble Commander are both free. Nimble Commander is also open source, so it cannot be re-priced out from under you — worth weighing if the pricing change is what pushed you to look.

**Leave Path Finder if…**

- Recurring pricing for a file manager is the dealbreaker.
- You use maybe five of its features.
- You want your layout back automatically.
- You want the keyboard, not the toolbar.

**Keep Path Finder if…**

- You use its modules and browser panes.
- You want the deepest feature set, full stop.
- The yearly cost is not a real constraint.
- You need it today.
- Total Commander on a Mac
- Alternatives to Marta
- Alternatives to ForkLift
- Diptychon vs all four, side by side

Path Finder does far more than Diptychon will ever do. This page argues about the pricing model and the footprint, not about who has more features — Path Finder wins that one outright.

# Docs (https://diptychon.com/docs/) — generated from the repository docs, guarded by tests

# Diptychon user guide

A task-by-task walkthrough. For the bare shortcut list, see
[keyboard-reference.md](keyboard-reference.md). Terms here follow
[`CONTEXT.md`](../CONTEXT.md) exactly — **Panel**, **Active/Inactive Panel**,
**Operation**, **Tag**.

---

## 1. The dual-Panel model

Diptychon shows two **Panels** side by side, each listing one directory. Exactly one is
the **Active Panel** (marked with an accent border) — it has focus and is the source of
keyboard-driven Operations. The other is the **Inactive Panel**.

- **Switch which Panel is Active:** `⇥` (Tab), or click into a Panel.
- **Why two?** So the source and the destination are both on screen. Moving files is a
  single gesture, not a copy-paste round trip through one window.

The **Destination** of an Operation is resolved *per gesture*, not fixed:

| Gesture | Destination |
|---------|-------------|
| Commander copy/move (`⌥⌘→/←`) | the **Inactive Panel** |
| Clipboard paste (`⌘V`) | the **Active Panel** |
| Drag & drop | wherever you drop |

---

## 2. Navigating

- **Open / enter:** `↩` or double-click. **Go up:** `⌘↑`.
- **Back / forward:** `⌘←` / `⌘→`. The bracket pair `⌘[` / `⌘]` still works as a
  US-layout alias — on a German keyboard `[` is ⌥8 5, so that chord can never match.
- **Path bar:** the breadcrumb above each Panel is clickable — jump to any ancestor.
  Paste an absolute path into Search and it navigates there directly.
- **Go to Folder:** `⇧⌘G`, then type or paste a path.
- **Sidebar:** `⌘B` shows/hides a left sidebar of places you pin. It's deliberately
  smaller than Finder's — just the jumping-off points people actually use.
- **Show hidden files:** `⇧⌘.`.
- **Menu bar:** every command above also sits in the menus (**Go**, **File**, **View**),
  each labelled with *your* current binding — handy while the chords are still new.

---

## 3. Selecting

Selection is independent of opening. Use `⌘A` (all), `⎋` (none), `⇧⌘I` (invert), plus
the usual click / `⇧`-click / `⌘`-click. Most Operations act on the **selection** if
there is one, otherwise on the item under the cursor.

---

## 4. Moving & copying files

**The Commander way (across Panels):** point the Inactive Panel at your destination,
select in the Active Panel, then:

- `⌥⌘→` / `⌥⌘←` — **copy** the selection into the Inactive Panel.
- `⌥⇧⌘→` / `⌥⇧⌘←` — **move** it instead.

**The Finder way (clipboard):** `⌘C` to copy, `⌘V` to paste into the Active Panel, or
`⌥⌘V` to paste-move. Also: `⌘D` duplicate, `⌘⌫` move to Trash, `⇧⌘N` new folder,
`⌃⌘N` new file.

**Name collisions** are caught *before* anything is written — you choose overwrite,
keep-both, or skip.

---

## 5. Undo — the safety net

Every file Operation records its own inverse, so **`⌘Z` undoes multi-level** across
move / copy / trash / rename, and `⇧⌘Z` redoes. Each undo/redo flashes a **toast**
naming exactly what was reversed ("Undone — Moved 12 items"), so blind `⌘Z` never
leaves you guessing.

**The one exception: overwrites.** When an Operation overwrites an existing file, the
original is gone — that can't be reversed. Diptychon says so honestly ("Can't undo — files
were overwritten") rather than offering a misleading undo.

---

## 6. Finder tags

`⌘T` opens tagging for the selection. These are **real Apple Finder tags** stored on the
file — set one here and it shows in Finder; tag in Finder and it shows here. Diptychon
keeps **no parallel tag system**. You can also **filter a Panel by tag** to focus on
just the tagged items.

---

## 7. Staging — collect, then act

Staging is a virtual set you fill from anywhere, then operate on as a group — useful when
the files you care about are scattered across folders.

- **Add selection to Staging:** `⇧⌘S`.
- **Show/hide the Staging panel:** `⇧⌘B`.
- **Remove from Staging:** `⌫` while the Staging panel is focused.

Staging collects *references* to files — it doesn't move or copy anything until you run
an Operation on the staged set.

---

## 8. Previewing & inspecting

- **QuickLook:** `␣` — the same floating preview as Finder.
- **Inline preview / inspector pane:** a dockable pane showing the selected item's
  preview and details, for when you want it always-on rather than a spacebar pop.
- **Get Info:** `⌘I`. **Reveal in Finder:** `⇧⌘R`. **Open With…:** `⌘↩`.
  **Copy path(s):** `⌥⌘C`.

---

## 9. Renaming

- **One file, inline:** `⌘R` renames in place.
- **Many files, batch:** the batch-rename tool offers multiple modes (find/replace,
  numbering, etc.) with a **live preview** so you see the result before committing.

---

## 10. Drag & drop

Drag within a Panel, between Panels, and **to/from Finder** — Diptychon interoperates
with the rest of the system rather than being a walled garden.

---

## 11. The command palette

`⌘K` opens the command palette: start typing an action's name and run it with `↩`. Every
action shows its keyboard shortcut next to it, so the palette doubles as a discovery
tool while you learn the chords.

---

## 12. Finding files — Search and Filter are different tools

Two fields, two jobs. Mixing them up is the most common early confusion:

| | `⌘F` **Search** | `⇧⌘F` **Filter** |
|---|---|---|
| Where it looks | recursively, from your Home folder | the Active Panel's current folder |
| What it's for | "where did I put that?" | "narrow what I'm looking at" |
| Matching | fuzzy — typed letters in order, not a substring | name contains |

Search also understands paths: type or paste an absolute path (or one starting with
`~`) and the Panel navigates there instead of searching. Matching a folder in the
path counts, so `proj/inv` finds `Projects/invoices`. Hidden files stay out unless
you flip the eye toggle.

---

## 13. The embedded terminal

`⌘J` opens a terminal across the bottom of both Panels, already `cd`-ed into the
**Active Panel's** folder — no copying paths around. `⌘J` again hides it; the shell
keeps running.

---

## 14. Gadgets — bring your own tools

A gadget runs an external app or command-line tool against your selection, straight
from the command palette. They are **declarative** — a JSON entry, no plugin API and
no scripting language, which is deliberate: the tool stays inspectable.

`⌘K → "Gadgets: Edit Config…"` writes a working starter on first use. Full syntax and
examples: [gadgets.md](gadgets.md).

---

## 15. Watching long operations

Copying a large folder doesn't block the app. The **Activity** pane (the list icon in
the header) shows what's running and lets you cancel it; progress also surfaces as a
toast. Diptychon deliberately has no background queue yet — one Operation runs at a
time, and that's visible rather than hidden.

---

## 16. What Diptychon doesn't do (on purpose)

- **No remote / cloud mounts** (SFTP, S3, WebDAV) — Diptychon is local-first.
- **No archive-as-folder**, no folder **sync/compare**.
- **A restrained sidebar** — less than Finder's, by design.

These keep the app light. If remote server access is your core job, a tool like ForkLift
is the better fit — Diptychon is the light, reliable, native dual-Panel for **local** work.

---

*See also:* [keyboard-reference.md](keyboard-reference.md) ·
[../README.md](../README.md) · [../CONTEXT.md](../CONTEXT.md) (domain vocabulary).

---

# Keyboard reference

Every default shortcut in Diptychon, grouped by task. Bindings are **data-driven**:
they come from `Keymap.default` (`Sources/Diptychon/Operations/Keymap.swift`), the same
table the app dispatches against.

This file used to *claim* it was generated from that table and then drift anyway — it
documented `⌘[` for history months after ⌘← took over, and missed eleven bindings.
`DocsKeyboardReferenceTests` now checks both directions on every test run: no binding
missing here, nothing here that the app doesn't dispatch. When it fails it prints the
correct table.

> Notation: `⌃` Control · `⌥` Option · `⇧` Shift · `⌘` Command — always in that order,
> matching what the menus and the shortcut editor show. `↩` Return · `␣` Space ·
> `⇥` Tab · `⌫` Delete/Backspace · `⎋` Escape.

**Everything below can be rebound** in Settings (`⌘,`) → Shortcuts, except the
structural keys `⇥`, `↩`, `␣`, `⌫` and `⎋`, which navigation and selection depend on.
The menus show your *current* binding, not the default.

## Panels & navigation

| Shortcut | Action |
|----------|--------|
| `⇥` | Switch the Active Panel |
| `↩` | Open the selected folder/file |
| `⌘↑` | Go up (leave the current directory) |
| `⌘←` | Back in this panel's history |
| `⌘→` | Forward in this panel's history |
| `⌘[` | Back — US-layout alias |
| `⌘]` | Forward — US-layout alias |
| `⇧⌘G` | Go to Folder (type a path) |
| `⇧⌘.` | Show/hide hidden files |
| `⌘B` | Show/hide the sidebar |

> History runs on ⌘←/⌘→ because they work on every keyboard layout. The bracket pair is
> kept as an alias for US layouts — on a German layout `[` is ⌥5, so that chord can
> never match.

## Search & filter

| Shortcut | Action |
|----------|--------|
| `⌘F` | Focus **Search** — recursive, from the sidebar |
| `⇧⌘F` | Focus **Filter** — narrows the Active Panel's current folder |

## Selection

| Shortcut | Action |
|----------|--------|
| `⌘A` | Select all |
| `⎋` | Clear selection |
| `⇧⌘I` | Invert selection |

## Commander gestures (across Panels)

The Active Panel is the source; the Inactive Panel is the destination. The arrow
direction is simply which side is inactive.

| Shortcut | Action |
|----------|--------|
| `⌥⌘→` / `⌥⌘←` | **Copy** the Active selection into the Inactive Panel |
| `⌥⇧⌘→` / `⌥⇧⌘←` | **Move** the Active selection into the Inactive Panel |

## File operations

| Shortcut | Action |
|----------|--------|
| `⌘C` | Copy to clipboard |
| `⌘V` | Paste (copy) into the Active Panel |
| `⌥⌘V` | Paste-**move** into the Active Panel |
| `⌘D` | Duplicate |
| `⌘⌫` | Move to Trash |
| `⌘R` | Rename (inline for one item, batch sheet for several) |
| `⇧⌘N` | New folder |
| `⌃⌘N` | New file |
| `⌘Z` | Undo the last operation |
| `⇧⌘Z` | Redo |

> Undo is multi-level and reversible across move/copy/trash/rename. **Overwrites are
> the exception** — they destroy the original and cannot be undone; Diptychon tells you
> so rather than offering a misleading undo.

## Tags & staging

Staging is a holding pen: collect files from different folders, then operate on the
set as one.

| Shortcut | Action |
|----------|--------|
| `⌘T` | Show/edit Finder tags for the selection |
| `⇧⌘S` | Add the selection to Staging |
| `⇧⌘B` | Show/hide the Staging panel |
| `⌫` | Remove from Staging (when the Staging panel is focused — no disk delete) |

## View & tools

| Shortcut | Action |
|----------|--------|
| `␣` | QuickLook preview |
| `⌘I` | Get Info |
| `⌘↩` | Open With… |
| `⇧⌘R` | Reveal in Finder |
| `⌥⌘C` | Copy path(s) |
| `⌘J` | Show/hide the embedded terminal, opened in the Active Panel's folder |
| `⌘K` | Command palette (run any action by name) |

---

Prefer the mouse? Everything here is also reachable by click, context menu, the menu
bar, or the command palette (`⌘K`). See the **[user guide](user-guide.md)** for the
workflows these shortcuts serve.

---

# Gadgets — user-defined external-tool actions

Gadgets let you run an external app or command-line tool against the current
selection, straight from the ⌘K command palette (issue 36). They are
**declarative** — no plugin API, no scripting language; that's the product line.

## Quick start

1. **⌘K → "Gadgets: Edit Config…"** — creates the config with a working starter
   on first use and opens it in your editor.
2. Edit, save, then **⌘K → "Gadgets: Reload"** — it reports how many gadgets
   loaded and lists any config errors.
3. **Select one or more files**, then **⌘K, type the gadget's name, ↩**.

Example — a "Zip Selection" gadget:

```json
{
  "id": "zip-selection",
  "name": "Zip Selection",
  "type": "executable",
  "target": "/usr/bin/zip",
  "args": ["-r", "Diptychon-Test.zip", "${active.selection.names}"],
  "workingDirectory": "${active.folder.path}"
}
```

Select files → ⌘K → "zip" → ↩. The first run of an executable gadget shows a
one-time confirmation with the exact command; after that, `Diptychon-Test.zip`
appears in the active folder. A gadget that uses selection variables is greyed
out in the palette until something is selected — if a gadget looks disabled,
that's almost always why.

## Where gadgets live

`~/Library/Application Support/Diptychon/gadgets.json`

The easiest way in: open the palette (⌘K) and run **Gadgets: Edit Config…** —
it creates the file with a working starter on first use and opens it. After
editing, run **Gadgets: Reload** (also in the palette); it reports what loaded
and lists any config errors.

## Format

```json
{
  "gadgets": [
    {
      "id": "open-in-pixelmator",
      "name": "Open in Pixelmator",
      "type": "application",
      "target": "/Applications/Pixelmator Pro.app"
    },
    {
      "id": "optimize-pngs",
      "name": "Optimize PNGs",
      "type": "executable",
      "target": "/opt/homebrew/bin/oxipng",
      "args": ["-o", "4", "${active.selection.paths}"],
      "workingDirectory": "${active.folder.path}"
    }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes | Unique key. Also remembers the one-time run confirmation. |
| `name` | yes | The title shown in the palette (category "Gadgets"). |
| `type` | yes | `application` (open selection with an .app — a saved "Open With") or `executable` (run a binary). |
| `target` | yes | Path to the `.app` or binary. Single-value variables allowed. |
| `args` | no | argv template, `executable` only. |
| `workingDirectory` | no | Working dir, `executable` only. Single-value variables allowed. |

Top-level keys starting with `"//"` are ignored — use them for comments.
A malformed entry is skipped (and reported on reload) without dropping the rest.

## Substitution variables

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| `${active.selection.paths}` | Absolute paths of the selection — **multi-value** |
| `${active.selection.names}` | File names of the selection — **multi-value** |
| `${current.file.path}` | The first selected file's absolute path |
| `${active.folder.path}` | The active panel's folder |
| `${inactive.folder.path}` | The other panel's folder |
| `${user.home}` | Your home directory |

**Multi-value expansion is argv-safe:** an argument containing a multi-value
variable becomes one argv entry *per selected file* — `"--f=${active.selection.paths}"`
with two files selected becomes `--f=/a one.txt` and `--f=/b.txt`. Never a
space-joined string, so filenames with spaces need no quoting. Only one
multi-value variable per argument; unknown variables are an error, not passed
through.

A gadget that references selection variables is greyed in the palette until
something is selected. Application gadgets always act on the selection.

## Safety

- Executable gadgets run via an **argv array** — never through a shell, so a
  hostile filename can't inject commands.
- The **first run** of each executable gadget shows a confirmation with the
  exact expanded command (one-time per gadget id).
- Commands run with your own user privileges, same as Terminal. Output is not
  captured — gadgets are fire-and-forget.

## Out of scope (deliberate)

Scripting/plugin runtimes, capturing tool output, a GUI editor, hotkey binding
for gadgets (palette-only in v1 — the keymap's `AppAction` surface is static;
a follow-up issue covers binding if demand shows).
